text:
Doctor: Well, it looks like you're pregnant.
Woman: Oh my God, I'm pregnant?!
Doctor: No, it just looks like you are.
FP Edit: RIP my inbox
gist: A doctor says a woman looks pregnant, and when she rejoices he clarifies she only looks pregnant, meaning she is fat.

wordplay.explanation: 'it looks like you're pregnant' means 'apparently you are' and literally 'you appear pregnant'.

characters.looks: doctor in white coat, clipboard, deadpan
plump woman, hands on round belly, overjoyed then stunned

text:
I asked a pretty, young, homeless woman if I could take her home, and she said yes with a big smile.
The look on her face soon changed when I walked off with her cardboard box.
gist: A man asks a homeless woman if he can take her home, she agrees happily, and he walks off with her cardboard box.

wordplay.explanation: 'Take her home' as bring her to his house vs carry away her home, the box.

characters.looks: smug man carrying a cardboard box
young homeless woman, worn coat, smile fading

adaptNote: rephrase so the question can mean taking her dwelling

text:
Cop on horse says to little girl on bike, "Did Santa get you that?"
"Yes," replies the little girl.
"Well tell him to put a reflector light on it next year!" and fines her $5.
The little girl looks up at the cop and says, "Nice horse you've got there, did Santa bring you that?"
The cop chuckles and replies, "He sure did!"
"Well," says the little girl, "Next year tell Santa that the d*ck goes under the horse, not on top of it!"
gist: Mounted cop fines a little girl for a bike without a reflector and mocks it as Santa's gift; she retorts that Santa put the dick on top of the horse instead of under it, calling the cop a dick.

wordplay.explanation: 'dick' means both a horse's penis (which belongs under the horse) and a jerk (the cop sitting on top).

characters.looks: mounted police officer, uniform, helmet, smug grin, ticket pad
little girl, pigtails, small bicycle, sharp unimpressed look
jolly bearded old man, red suit, white fur trim
tall brown police horse, saddle, calm

adaptNote: Use 'осёл' (donkey/idiot): tell Ded Moroz the donkey goes under the saddle, not on it.

text:
A man is showing off his new apartment...
After a night at the bar, he brings his friends up, where he has large brass gong and a mallet.
"What's with the gong and mallet?" One of his friends asked.
"It's not a gong, it's a talking clock," the man replied.
"A talking clock? Seriously?"
"Yup."
"How's it work?" The friend asked
"Watch," said the man. He picked up the mallet and banged the gong as hard as he could, stepping back as the pound reverberated around the room.
The friends looked at the man, rather confused.
Suddenly, someone on the other side of the wall started screaming "You bastard! It's 3 in the morning!"
gist: Man shows friends his 'talking clock', a gong he bangs at night, and the furious neighbor screams the time through the wall.

characters.looks: tipsy proud man, rolled sleeves, holding mallet
puzzled tipsy friend, jacket, raised eyebrow
unseen voice behind wall, angry pajama silhouette

text:
A girl once told me, “If you lost about 50 pounds you’d be cute”
I told her, “if I lost 50 pounds I’d be talking to your friends!”
gist: A woman says he would be cute if he lost weight, and he retorts that then he would be talking to her prettier friends.

young woman, condescending look, drink in hand

text:
I went to the doctors recently He said: “Don’t eat anything fatty” I said: “What, like bacon and burgers?”
He said, “No. Fatty, don’t eat anything."
gist: Doctor's advice 'don't eat anything fatty' turns out to be 'Fatty, don't eat anything', addressed to the patient.

wordplay.explanation: 'Anything fatty' (fatty food) re-parsed as 'Fatty' (insulting address) + 'don't eat anything'.

blunt doctor in white coat with clipboard
